name: U04 - Brep: What is it?
context:
2- Brep: What is it?

"The word Brep stands for Boundary Representation. That in itself doesn't tell you much, but allow me to break down the general idea behind Breps. In Rhino UI itself, we don't use the word Brep, that one is only for programmers. Instead "Polysurface" is used, but it is not an ideal replacement because a Brep may well have only a single surface."
- David Rutten

Source:

http://www.grasshopper3d.com/forum/topics/how-to-make-a-brep

- In Grasshopper, a Brep is a NURB

solution_principle:
2- Brep: What is it?

"The word Brep stands for Boundary Representation. That in itself doesn't tell you much, but allow me to break down the general idea behind Breps. In Rhino UI itself, we don't use the word Brep, that one is only for programmers. Instead "Polysurface" is used, but it is not an ideal replacement because a Brep may well have only a single surface."
- David Rutten

Source:

http://www.grasshopper3d.com/forum/topics/how-to-make-a-brep

- In Grasshopper, a Brep is a NURBS goemetry, and not a Mesh.

What is modeled in Rhino is a Surface or a Polysurface or a Mesh.

When a Polysurface is being referenced in Grasshopper, it would be called as a Brep and not a polysurface.

- The "Mesh Brep" component converts a Brep into a Mesh.

"NOTE: it is generally much easier to convert from a NURBS geometry to a mesh object rather than the other way around. While the UV coordinates of a NURBS surface are straightforward to convert to quad faces of a mesh, the opposite is not necessarily true, since a mesh might contain a combination of triangles and quads in a way that is not simple to extract a UV coordinate system out of."

Source:
http://grasshopperprimer.com/en/1-foundations/1-6/3_Creating%20Meshes.html
